reasons: No test or other evidence is visible.
The reducer logic is simple and clearly organized.

terms.meaning: A function that takes the current state and an action, and returns the new state.
A function a component registers so it is told when shared data changes.
A scheduled action that runs after a set delay.
A named instruction, such as add or dismiss, that describes a change to make.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and limits
sections.what: Brings in the notice types and sets the rules that only one notice shows at a time and removal waits a long time.
sections.why: The one-notice limit is set in the code. The reason for the long delay is not stated.
sections.watch_out: Raising the limit lets notices pile up on screen.

sections.name: ToasterToast
sections.title: Notice type
sections.what: Defines a notice as the library notice type plus an id, title, description and optional action.
sections.why: Gives each notice a stable id so it can be updated or removed later.
sections.watch_out: The id must always be set, because later steps depend on it.

sections.name: actionTypes
sections.title: Action names
sections.what: Lists the four action names: add, update, dismiss and remove.
sections.why: Gives the reducer a fixed set of named instructions.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new action means updating the reducer too.

sections.name: genId, ActionType
sections.title: Id counter
sections.what: Creates a new unique id for each notice from a counter.
sections.why: Each notice must be found and changed later, so it needs its own id.
sections.watch_out: The counter is held in memory and restarts on page reload.

sections.name: Action
sections.title: Action shapes
sections.what: Describes each action and the data it carries. Dismiss and remove can name one notice or, when no id is given, all of them.
sections.why: Makes sure callers send the right data for each action.
sections.watch_out: A dismiss with no id closes every notice.

sections.name: State, toastTimeouts
sections.title: Notice state and timers
sections.what: Defines the state that holds the notice list, and a map of removal timers keyed by notice id.
sections.why: The timers let each notice be removed later, and tracking them avoids starting two timers for one notice.
sections.watch_out: A timer is cleared only when the notice is removed, so a dismissed notice keeps its timer until then.

sections.name: addToRemoveQueue
sections.title: Scheduling removal
sections.what: Starts a long timer that removes a dismissed notice, unless one is already running for that id.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the closing animation finish before the notice leaves memory.
sections.watch_out: The delay is very long, so dismissed notices stay in memory for a long time.

sections.name: reducer, memoryState
sections.title: Reducer and listener list
sections.what: Applies each action to the list: adds the new notice at the front, updates a matching notice, marks notices closed on dismiss, and removes notices. Holds the current list and the set of listeners.
sections.why: Keeps all changes to the notice list in one place.
sections.watch_out: The dismiss branch also starts removal timers. The code comment flags this side effect, and it is easy to break when editing.

sections.name: dispatch, Toast
sections.title: Dispatch and notice type
sections.what: Runs an action through the reducer, stores the new list, and tells every listening component. Also defines the notice type for callers.
sections.why: This is the single entry point for every change to the list.
sections.watch_out: A component that has not registered as a listener will not see changes.

sections.name: toast
sections.title: Toast function
sections.what: Creates a new notice with a fresh id, and returns its id plus functions to dismiss or update it. The notice opens right away and closes when its open flag is set to false.
sections.why: Gives callers a simple way to show a notice and control it afterward.
sections.watch_out: Because only one notice is kept, each new call replaces the one showing.

sections.name: useToast
sections.title: useToast hook
sections.what: Lets a component read the current list and receive changes. Registers the component as a listener on mount and removes it on exit. Returns the list, the toast function and a dismiss function.
sections.why: Lets the Toaster redraw whenever notices change.
sections.watch_out: The effect re-subscribes after every change. It works, but is more work than needed.

summary: Keeps the list of pop-up notices in one shared place and provides functions to add, update, dismiss and remove them.
purpose: Lets any part of the app call toast() to show a notice, and lets the Toaster draw them.
why: The code holds one shared list in memory and changes it through a reducer, a common pattern for shared state. The reasons for the one-notice limit and the long removal delay are not stated.
how: Each notice gets a unique id. Add, update, dismiss and remove actions all go to one reducer, which returns the new list. The reducer keeps only the newest notice. Dismissing schedules a timer to remove the notice later. After each change the hook tells every listening component the new list. The useToast hook lets components read the list and call toast or dismiss.
inputs: Notice content from callers: title, description, optional action and variant.
outputs: The notice list, plus the toast, dismiss and update functions.
risks: Only one notice is kept, so each new one replaces the last. Removal waits about 16 minutes, so dismissed notices stay in memory that long. The list is in memory only, so a page reload clears it.
debug: If a notice does not appear, check that Toaster is mounted and reads this list. If notices vanish or pile up, check TOAST_LIMIT and TOAST_REMOVE_DELAY. If a notice never leaves the list, check the removal timer.
